uk7wwhXdWYHKKZ8KTCVw:hook.text: This crab is guarding a clutch of eggs. And they aren't even his.

uk7wwhXdWYHKKZ8KTCVw:kiwi.text: This is Kiwi. He's a shore crab.

uk7wwhXdWYHKKZ8KTCVw:toffee.text: And this speck is Toffee. She's a barnacle. Not that you'd ever guess.

uk7wwhXdWYHKKZ8KTCVw:land.text: She lands on Kiwi and finds a soft spot in his shell.

uk7wwhXdWYHKKZ8KTCVw:needle.text: She sheds her own shell, pushes a tiny hollow needle through... and injects herself.

uk7wwhXdWYHKKZ8KTCVw:roots.text: Inside Kiwi, she grows roots. Through his whole body. And drinks from his blood.

uk7wwhXdWYHKKZ8KTCVw:fine.text: Kiwi looks fine. But he'll never have babies of his own.

uk7wwhXdWYHKKZ8KTCVw:months.text: Months later, a sac pushes out under his tail flap. Right where a mother crab carries her eggs.

uk7wwhXdWYHKKZ8KTCVw:body.text: And Kiwi's body changes. His narrow tail flap grows wide and round, the shape a mother crab has.

uk7wwhXdWYHKKZ8KTCVw:claws.text: His claws stay small. Scientists think the wide flap shelters the sac.

uk7wwhXdWYHKKZ8KTCVw:males.text: Tiny male larvae slip into the sac... and it fills with eggs. Toffee's eggs.

uk7wwhXdWYHKKZ8KTCVw:still.text: Kiwi is still a boy. But now he behaves like a mother.

uk7wwhXdWYHKKZ8KTCVw:care.text: He cleans the sac. He guards it. He treats Toffee's eggs as his own.

uk7wwhXdWYHKKZ8KTCVw:launch.text: When the larvae are ready, he climbs up high... and bobs... and fans.

uk7wwhXdWYHKKZ8KTCVw:cloud.text: A cloud of baby barnacles, off to find crabs of their own.

uk7wwhXdWYHKKZ8KTCVw:turn.text: Toffee doesn't just take Kiwi's food. She takes his whole job of making babies... and hands him hers.

uk7wwhXdWYHKKZ8KTCVw:end.text: And Kiwi raises them all. Brood after brood.

uk7wwhXdWYHKKZ8KTCVw:life.text: For the rest of his life, Toffee is part of him.

uk7wwhXdWYHKKZ8KTCVw:shell.text: And now the sac is out, he'll never shed his shell again. Never grow.
